# Chapter Nine: The Refinery Ambush

> *"When panic takes the wheel, you don't fight the skid. You put your foot through the floorboard and steer into the crash."*

The lower geothermal refinery was a cavern of rusted steel, howling steam pipes, and molten slag vats.

Gracie, Kael, and Tess stood on an open catwalk suspended fifty feet above the glowing magma runoff. There was no coolant waiting for them. There were no runners.

There were only twenty Black Sun mercenaries stepping out from behind the steam boilers, assault rifles leveled.

Leading them was a hulking cybernetic enforcer with dual heavy blasters mounted to his forearms. On the overhead gantry stood Jax, clutching a heavy satchel of syndicate credit chips with a trembling, apologetic grin.

“Sorry, Gracie!” Jax shouted over the roar of the steam vents. “Baron Vargas offered ten million credits for you and the precursor core! A guy’s gotta look out for his retirement!”

Inside Gracie’s skull, the Box suffered a catastrophic psychological collapse.

*NO! NO! NO!* the passenger screamed, a hysterical, guilt-ridden wail that felt like a drill puncturing Gracie's eardrum. *I WAS WRONG! I GOT US KILLED! THEY'RE GOING TO TAKE US BACK! THE NEEDLES! THE STRAPS! SHOOT THE FUEL PIPES! BLOW US ALL TO HELL! BURN US! BURN US NOW!*

The blinding panic hit Gracie like a physical blow. She fell to one knee, clutching her skull as scarlet neural feedback washed over her vision.

“Gracie!” Kael yelled, raising his heavy slug-rifle and firing into the nearest mercenary, blowing him off the catwalk.

Tess scrambled behind a reinforced support pillar, deploying her three combat drones in a frantic defensive perimeter. “We’re pinned! We can’t get back to the lift!”

Heavy kinetic rounds chewed into the metal catwalk around them. 

*WE'RE GOING TO DIE ON THE TABLE!* the Box sobbed, completely unhinged. *END IT! EAT A BULLET!*

“Shut... the hell... up!” Gracie snarled through clenched teeth, blood dripping from her nose. She forced her eyes open, locking her focus on the ceiling above the mercenaries. “Listen to me, you coward! I dragged us out of Vengeance’s dungeon through a garbage chute three months ago! We survived a hundred years of his hell! We are NOT dying in this filthy ditch because some rat sold us out!”

The fierce, unbreakable conviction in her thoughts hit the passenger like a bucket of ice water. The hysterical wailing stuttered, then stopped.

*The... the steam vents...* the passenger whispered, its tone suddenly shifting from panic to cold, desperate clarity. *Main pressure valve forty-two... above the enforcer's head... an emergency blowout will flash-fry their optics...*

“Tess!” Gracie roared, drawing both plasma pistols. “Target the yellow relief valve above the leader! Drone strike, NOW!”

Tess’s drones buzzed upward into the gloom, firing miniature shaped charges into the rusted valve.

*BOOM.*

Superheated steam erupted from the fractured pipe in a deafening, blinding hurricane. The mercenaries shrieked as 600-degree vapor engulfed their positions, short-circuiting their cybernetic targeting HUDs.

“Move!” Gracie shouted. 

Vaulting over the railing, Gracie slid beneath the blinded enforcer, firing twin plasma bolts upward into his unarmored power pack. The cybernetic brute exploded in an arc of blue electricity.

Kael and Tess charged across the catwalk behind her, gunning down the disoriented cartel goons as they fought their way back toward the service elevator. 

As the lift doors slammed shut, cutting off the gunfire, Gracie slumped against the wall, chest heaving.

*I'm sorry,* the voice in her head whispered softly, trembling with shame. *I gave you bad advice...*

Gracie wiped the blood from her nose and let out a dry, ragged laugh. “You did. But you fixed it. We’re even, ghost.”
